Blog Post Title: Declined for Credit in South Africa? 7 Reasons and What to Do Next
Meta description: Declined for a loan, store card or car finance? The 7 most common reasons South Africans are declined, how to find out which one applies to you, and what to do next.
Meta Image Alt text: Woman on the phone after being declined for credit
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**Most South Africans who are declined for credit are turned down for one of seven reasons: missed payments, a judgment or default listing, too much debt for their income, too many recent applications, a debt review flag, no credit history, or wrong information on their credit report. You have the right to ask the lender for the main reason in writing, and your free credit report shows you the rest.**

## The 7 most common reasons for being declined

1. **Missed or late payments.** Your payment profile shows how you have paid each account month by month. A few recent missed payments weigh more than old ones.
2. **A default or judgment.** Listings like "handed over", "default" or a civil judgment tell lenders an account went badly wrong.
3. **Your income cannot carry another repayment.** Lenders must do an affordability assessment by law. If your existing repayments and living costs already take most of your salary, you will be declined even with a clean record.
4. **Too many recent applications.** Every time a lender checks your record for an application, an enquiry is added. Many enquiries in a short time look like you are desperate for credit.
5. **A debt review flag.** While you are under debt review, lenders may not give you new credit.
6. **No credit history.** If you have never had an account in your name, lenders have nothing to judge you on.
7. **Wrong information.** An account that is not yours, a paid account still showing a balance, or a duplicate listing can sink an application that should have been approved.

## How to find out which one applies to you

Under section 62 of the National Credit Act, you can ask the lender for the main reason your application was declined. If the reason was your credit report, they must also tell you which credit bureau they used. Ask in writing, by email if you can, so you have a record.

Then get your free report from that bureau. You are entitled to one free report a year from each bureau. Our guide on [how to check your credit report for free](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa) shows you how.

## What each reason means for you

| Reason | Can it be fixed? | First step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrong information | Yes, often within weeks | Dispute it with the bureau for free |
| Missed payments | Improves with time | Bring accounts up to date and keep them there |
| Default or judgment | Sometimes | Check the dates and whether it is paid |
| Affordability | Yes | Pay down balances before applying again |
| Too many enquiries | Yes, with time | Stop applying for a few months |
| Debt review flag | After clearance | Finish the process and get your clearance certificate |
| No credit history | Yes | Start small and pay on time |

## What not to do after a decline

- Do not apply at three more lenders the same week. Each application adds an enquiry and makes the next decline more likely.
- Do not pay anyone who promises to "remove you from the blacklist". There is no blacklist, and accurate information cannot be removed early. Read [what "blacklisted" really means](https://clearmy.name/blog/am-i-blacklisted-south-africa).
- Do not ignore the reason. A decline is useful information about what to fix.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does being declined lower my credit score?

The decline itself is not listed, but the application adds an enquiry. One enquiry has little effect. Many in a short time can lower your score.

### Must the lender tell me why I was declined?

Yes. If you ask, the lender must give you the main reason in writing, and if it was your credit report, name the bureau it used (National Credit Act, section 62).

### How long should I wait before applying again?

Fix the reason first. For most people that means at least three months without new applications while they bring accounts up to date.

Blog Post Title: How to Check Your Credit Report for Free in South Africa
Meta description: You can get your credit report free once a year from every credit bureau in South Africa. Where to get it from TransUnion, Experian, XDS and VeriCred, and what to look for.
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**Every South African can get one free credit report a year from each registered credit bureau. Request it online from TransUnion, Experian, XDS and VeriCred. Checking your own report does not lower your score.**

## Where to get your free report

Section 72 of the National Credit Act gives you the right to a free credit report once a year from every credit bureau. The four main consumer bureaus are:

- **TransUnion:** [transunion.co.za](https://www.transunion.co.za/education/credit-report)
- **Experian:** [experian.co.za](https://www.experian.co.za/consumer)
- **XDS:** [xds.co.za](https://www.xds.co.za)
- **VeriCred:** [vccb.co.za](https://www.vccb.co.za/FreeCreditReportNotice)

You will need your ID number and to answer a few security questions. Most bureaus email the report as a PDF.

## Which bureau should you check first?

If you were declined, start with the bureau the lender used. Ask the lender which one it was. If you were not declined and just want to check, start with TransUnion and Experian, which most banks use, then check the others. Each bureau can hold slightly different information, which is also why [your scores differ](https://clearmy.name/why-credit-scores-differ).

## What to look for on your report

1. **Personal details.** Check your name, ID number, addresses and employer. An address you never lived at can be a sign of fraud.
2. **Accounts.** Make sure every account is yours and the balances are right.
3. **Payment profile.** Look for months marked as missed when you know you paid.
4. **Adverse listings.** Look for words like "default", "handed over" or "written off", and check the dates.
5. **Judgments and notices.** Check that any judgment is yours and has not been paid or rescinded.
6. **Enquiries.** Check you recognise every company that looked at your record.

Our guide to [understanding your credit report](https://clearmy.name/understanding-your-credit-report) explains each section in more detail.

## Does checking my report hurt my score?

No. Checking your own report is not a credit application, so it does not count against you. You can check as often as you like. Only the first report each year from each bureau is free.

## Found something wrong?

Disputing wrong information with a bureau is free. The bureau must investigate, and the lender must prove the information is correct. If they cannot, it must be corrected or removed. If several things look wrong, or you are not sure what you are looking at, upload your report and we will sort it for you.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the free credit report really free?

Yes. The law gives you one free report a year from each registered credit bureau. You only pay if you want more than one report a year from the same bureau.

### Do I need to check all four bureaus?

It is worth it. Lenders use different bureaus, and an error can sit on one report and not the others.

### How long does it take to get my report?

Online requests are usually immediate or same day once you have passed the security questions.

Blog Post Title: What Is a Good Credit Score in South Africa? Scores by Bureau
Meta description: What counts as a good credit score in South Africa depends on the bureau. TransUnion and Experian score ranges explained, what lenders look for, and how to move up a band.
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**On TransUnion's scale of 0 to 999, a score of 681 or more is good and 767 or more is excellent. Experian uses a different scale that runs up to 740, so the same score means different things at different bureaus. Always check which bureau a score comes from before you compare it.**

## TransUnion score bands

TransUnion is one of the largest bureaus in South Africa. Its consumer score runs from 0 to 999, in these bands:

| Score | Band |
| --- | --- |
| 767 to 999 | Excellent |
| 681 to 766 | Good |
| 614 to 680 | Favourable |
| 583 to 613 | Average |
| 527 to 582 | Below average |
| 487 to 526 | Unfavourable |
| 0 to 486 | Poor |

TransUnion reported an average South African score of about 612 in 2025, which sits in the average band.

## Experian and other bureaus

Experian's score runs to 740, so a score of 620 is a solid result at Experian but only favourable at TransUnion. XDS and VeriCred use their own models too. This is why [your scores differ between bureaus](https://clearmy.name/why-credit-scores-differ), and why you should compare a score with that bureau's own bands.

## What lenders actually look at

Your score is a summary. Lenders also look at the detail behind it:

- whether you are paying your current accounts on time
- any defaults, judgments or debt review flags
- how much of your available credit you are using
- how many applications you have made recently
- whether your income can carry the new repayment

So a good score with an unaffordable repayment can still be declined, and a fair score with strong affordability can be approved.

## How to move up a band

1. Fix wrong information first. A wrong default can cost you a whole band.
2. Pay every account on time, every month. Payment history carries the most weight.
3. Bring balances down, especially on credit cards and store cards near their limits.
4. Stop applying for new credit for a few months.

For a full plan, read [how to improve your credit score in 90 days](https://clearmy.name/blog/improve-credit-score-90-days).

## Frequently asked questions

### What credit score do I need for a home loan?

There is no fixed cut-off, and each bank sets its own rules. Most home loan applicants are in the good to excellent bands, with strong affordability and a clean recent payment record.

### What credit score do I need for car finance?

Again it depends on the lender. Recent missed payments, judgments and affordability usually matter more than the exact number.

### Why does my score keep changing?

Scores update as lenders report new information each month, such as payments, balances and new enquiries.

Blog Post Title: Am I Blacklisted? What "Blacklisted" Really Means in South Africa
Meta description: There is no blacklist in South Africa. What lenders mean when they say you are blacklisted, how to find out what is on your record, and how to fix it without paying a scammer.
Meta Image Alt text: Woman reading a letter about her credit record
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**There is no blacklist in South Africa. When people say they are "blacklisted", they usually mean their credit report has a default, a judgment, a debt review flag or a history of missed payments. Each of these has its own rules for how long it stays and how it can be fixed.**

## What people mean by "blacklisted"

Credit bureaus keep a record of how you have paid your accounts. Lenders read that record and decide for themselves. Being "blacklisted" usually means one or more of these is on your record:

- **Adverse classifications** such as "slow payer", "default" or "handed over"
- **A civil judgment** granted against you by a court
- **A debt review flag**, if you have applied for debt counselling
- **An administration or sequestration order**
- **A poor payment profile** with many missed months

## How to find out what is on your record

Get your free credit report from each bureau. Our guide on [checking your credit report for free](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa) shows you where. Then look at the adverse listings, judgments and payment profile sections.

## Can a listing be removed?

It depends on whether it is right:

| The listing is | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong | Dispute it for free. If the lender cannot prove it, it must be removed. |
| Older than the law allows | It must be removed. Dispute it if it is still showing. |
| Accurate and recent | It stays for its legal period. Nobody can lawfully remove it early. |

How long each type stays is set by the National Credit Regulations. We cover the periods in [how long bad credit stays on your record](https://clearmy.name/blog/how-long-negative-information-stays-credit-report).

## Watch out for "unblacklisting" scams

Anyone who promises to "remove you from the blacklist" for a fee is selling something that does not exist. Disputing wrong information is free, and accurate information cannot be bought off your record. A legitimate credit repair provider may not take payment before the work is done. Read [how to choose a credit repair company](https://clearmy.name/choosing-a-credit-repair-company) before you pay anyone.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I get credit if I am "blacklisted"?

Possibly. It depends on what the listing is, how old it is, and your affordability. Some lenders still approve people with older adverse listings if recent payments are good.

### Does paying the account remove the listing?

Paying in full improves your record, and a paid judgment must be removed. An adverse classification for a paid account may still show until its period ends, but it will show as paid.

### How do I check if I am blacklisted for free?

Get your free annual credit report from each bureau and check the adverse listings and judgments sections.

Blog Post Title: No Credit History? How to Build a Credit Record in South Africa
Meta description: Declined because you have no credit history? How to build a credit record from scratch in South Africa, safely and cheaply, in the first 6 to 12 months.
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**If you have never had credit in your name, lenders have nothing to judge you on, so they often say no. You build a record by having one or two small accounts in your name and paying them on time every month for 6 to 12 months. Start small, keep balances low and never miss a payment.**

## Why "no history" gets you declined

A lender's main question is "will this person pay us back?". Your credit report answers it with your past behaviour. With no accounts, there is no answer, so many lenders decline or offer only small limits. This is common for young people, people who have always paid cash, and people whose accounts were in a partner's name.

## Ways to start a credit record

| Option | How it helps | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cellphone contract in your name | Reports monthly payments to the bureaus | Pick a contract you can easily afford for 24 months |
| Small store card | Easy to get, reports monthly | High interest if you carry a balance; pay it off each month |
| Entry-level credit card from your bank | Your bank already knows your income | Keep the limit low and the balance well below it |
| Accounts in your own name | Shows you on your record | Accounts in someone else's name do not build yours |

## The habits that build a good record

1. **Pay on time, every month.** Set up a debit order for at least the minimum.
2. **Use a small part of your limit.** Try to keep balances under about a third of the limit.
3. **Keep your first accounts open.** The age of your accounts helps over time.
4. **Apply slowly.** One new account every few months, not five at once.
5. **Check your report.** After six months, get your free report and make sure the accounts show and the payments are recorded. See [how to check it for free](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa).

## How long does it take?

Most people have a usable record after 6 months of on-time payments and a solid one after 12 months. For bigger applications such as [vehicle finance](https://clearmy.name/before-vehicle-finance) or a [home loan](https://clearmy.name/before-a-home-loan), lenders also want proof of stable income, so start building early.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does paying rent or utilities build my credit record?

Usually not, unless the landlord or provider reports to a credit bureau. Accounts with registered credit providers are what count.

### Will a store card hurt my score?

Not if you pay on time and keep the balance low. Missed payments and maxed-out cards are what hurt.

### Should I take out a loan just to build credit?

No. Start with a small account you would use anyway, such as a cellphone contract or a store card you pay off monthly.

Blog Post Title: How to Improve Your Credit Score in 90 Days: A Step-by-Step Plan
Meta description: A practical 90-day plan to improve your credit score in South Africa: fix errors, catch up on payments, lower balances and stop applying. What changes quickly and what takes time.
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**In 90 days you can usually fix wrong information, bring accounts up to date, lower your balances and stop new enquiries building up. Those four steps are what move a score fastest. Accurate negative history takes longer and falls away only with time.**

## Days 1 to 30: find and fix errors

1. Get your free report from each bureau. See [how to get it for free](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa).
2. List anything wrong: accounts that are not yours, paid accounts showing a balance, months marked missed that you paid, duplicates, and listings older than the law allows.
3. Dispute each error with the bureau. It is free. The lender must prove the information or it must be corrected.

Corrections often show within 20 business days, and a removed wrong default can lift your score more than anything else.

## Days 31 to 60: get every account up to date

- Pay any arrears on accounts that are still active, starting with the smallest ones you can clear completely.
- Set debit orders for at least the minimum on every account so nothing is missed again.
- If you cannot afford all your repayments, talk to us before you stop paying anything.

## Days 61 to 90: lower balances and stop applying

- Pay down credit cards and store cards, aiming for balances under about a third of each limit.
- Do not close old accounts that are paid up. Their history helps you.
- Make no new credit applications. Enquiries stay on your record for up to a year.

## What changes quickly and what takes time

| Item | How fast it changes |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong information removed | Weeks |
| Lower balances | Next monthly update |
| On-time payments | Builds month by month |
| Enquiries | Fall away after a year |
| Accurate defaults and judgments | Stay for their legal period, see [how long bad credit stays](https://clearmy.name/blog/how-long-negative-information-stays-credit-report) |

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I improve my credit score in 30 days?

If the problem is wrong information or high balances, yes, you can see a change in a month. Building a payment history takes longer.

### Will paying off a default raise my score?

It helps, because lenders see the account as paid. The listing may still show until its period ends.

### Should I pay a company to fix my score?

Disputes are free to do yourself. If you use a company, it may not charge you before the work is done.

Blog Post Title: How Long Does Bad Credit Stay on Your Record in South Africa?
Meta description: How long enquiries, defaults, judgments, payment history and debt review stay on your credit report in South Africa, under the National Credit Regulations.
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**Under the National Credit Regulations, enquiries and adverse classifications such as "default" show for up to 1 year, your payment profile for up to 5 years, and civil judgments for up to 5 years or until they are rescinded, abandoned or paid. A debt review flag stays until a clearance certificate is issued.**

## The maximum periods

| Information | Maximum period |
| --- | --- |
| Enquiries | 1 year |
| Adverse classifications ("slow payer", "default", "handed over") | 1 year |
| Payment profile | 5 years |
| Civil judgments | 5 years, or sooner if rescinded, abandoned or paid |
| Administration order | 5 years or until rescinded |
| Sequestration order | 5 years or until rehabilitation |
| Rehabilitation order | 5 years |
| Debt review flag | Until a clearance certificate is issued |
| Complaints you lodged | 6 months |

These are maximum periods, counted from the date of the event. Information may not be shown or used for scoring after its period ends.

## Paid-up judgments must be removed

Once you have paid the capital amount of a judgment, the credit provider must tell the bureaus, and the bureaus must update your record within 7 days of being told. If a paid judgment is still showing, dispute it. Our guide on [paid-up debt still on your credit report](https://clearmy.name/paid-up-debt-still-on-credit-report) walks you through it.

## Rules lenders must follow before listing you

- You must have missed at least three consecutive minimum payments before adverse information can be listed.
- You must be given notice before you are listed. If you settle the arrears within the notice period, you should not be listed.
- A debt that has prescribed may not be listed at all.

If any of these rules were broken, the listing can be disputed.

## What you can do now

1. Get your free reports and note the date of each negative item. See [how to check for free](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa).
2. Dispute anything older than its period, anything paid and still showing, and anything listed without notice.
3. For accurate, recent items, focus on paying on time from now on. See [the 90-day plan](https://clearmy.name/blog/improve-credit-score-90-days).

## Frequently asked questions

### Does a default stay for 5 years?

No. Adverse classifications like "default" show for up to 1 year. Your payment profile, which records the missed payments themselves, can show for up to 5 years.

### Does settling a debt clear my record immediately?

A paid judgment must be removed. Other listings show the account as paid but may remain until their period ends.

### Can I pay someone to remove a listing early?

Accurate information cannot lawfully be removed before its period ends. Only wrong or outdated information can be removed.

Blog Post Title: Under Debt Review? When You Can Get Credit Again
Meta description: Can you get credit while under debt review in South Africa? What the debt review flag means, how to get a clearance certificate, and how to rebuild your record after.
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**While you are under debt review you cannot take on new credit, and lenders can see the debt review flag on your record. The flag is removed once you receive a clearance certificate, usually after all debts in the process, other than a home loan, are paid. From then on, you rebuild your record like anyone else.**

## What the debt review flag means

When you apply for debt review, the bureaus are told and a flag is added to your record. The National Credit Regulator says this flag is not a "blacklisting". It tells lenders you are in a legal process to repay your debts, so they may not give you new credit while it is active.

## How the flag is removed

There are two lawful ways out:

1. **Clearance certificate.** Once all debts in the process are paid, other than a home loan, your debt counsellor issues a clearance certificate and the flag must be removed.
2. **Before a court order.** If no court order has been granted yet, you may be able to withdraw. Once an order is granted, only a court can end it before clearance.

Read [debt review removal](https://clearmy.name/debt-review-removal) and [checking your debt review status](https://clearmy.name/debt-review-status-and-clearance) for the details, and be wary of anyone promising a quick removal for a fee.

## Is the flag still showing after clearance?

Check each bureau after you get your clearance certificate. If the flag is still there, dispute it and attach the certificate. See [how to get your reports for free](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa).

## Rebuilding after debt review

- Start with one small account and pay it on time every month. Our guide on [building a credit record](https://clearmy.name/blog/build-credit-record-no-credit-history) shows how.
- Keep balances low and apply slowly.
- Give lenders 6 to 12 months of clean payments before a big application.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I get a loan while under debt review?

No new credit may be given while you are under debt review. A lender who gives you credit while you are under review may be lending recklessly.

### How long does debt review last?

Usually as long as it takes to repay the debts in the plan, often 3 to 5 years.

### Does debt review show on my credit report forever?

No. The flag must be removed once a clearance certificate is issued.

Blog Post Title: Declined for Car Finance? What to Fix Before You Apply Again
Meta description: Declined for vehicle finance in South Africa? Why banks decline car finance, what to check on your credit report, and how to get approved next time.
Meta Image Alt text: Couple looking at a new car
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**Car finance is usually declined for one of three reasons: recent missed payments, a default or judgment, or a repayment your income cannot carry. Ask the bank for the reason, get your free credit report, fix any errors, and lower your other debts before you apply again at one bank, not five.**

## Why banks decline vehicle finance

- **Affordability.** Banks add the car repayment, insurance and fuel to your existing debts and living costs. If the total is too high, the answer is no.
- **Recent payment problems.** Missed payments in the last 6 to 12 months count heavily.
- **Adverse listings or judgments.** See [what "blacklisted" really means](https://clearmy.name/blog/am-i-blacklisted-south-africa).
- **Too many applications.** Dealers often send your application to several banks at once. Each adds an enquiry.
- **Short credit history.** If you have never had credit, see [how to build a record](https://clearmy.name/blog/build-credit-record-no-credit-history).

## Before you apply again

1. Ask the bank for the main reason in writing. You are entitled to it. See [7 reasons you were declined](https://clearmy.name/blog/why-was-i-declined-for-credit).
2. Get your free reports and dispute anything wrong.
3. Bring every account up to date and pay down revolving balances.
4. Work out a repayment that fits your budget, including insurance.
5. Consider a bigger deposit or a cheaper car.
6. Apply once, through one dealer or your own bank, and ask the dealer not to send your application to every bank.

## Watch out for "no credit check" car deals

Rent-to-own and "blacklisted welcome" deals can cost far more over time. Read every contract, check who owns the car until the end, and check that the provider is registered with the National Credit Regulator if it is a credit agreement.

Our guide to [checking before vehicle finance](https://clearmy.name/before-vehicle-finance) has a full checklist.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long after being declined can I reapply for car finance?

Fix the reason first. For most people that takes at least three months.

### Does a bigger deposit help?

Yes. It lowers the amount and the repayment, which helps affordability.

### Will applying at several dealers hurt me?

Yes, if each one runs a credit check. Many enquiries in a short time can lower your score.

Blog Post Title: Store Cards, Buy Now Pay Later and Your Credit Score This Festive Season
Meta description: Thinking of opening store cards or using buy now pay later this festive season? How they affect your credit score in South Africa and how to avoid a January debt hangover.
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**Store cards and some buy now pay later services can help your credit record if you pay on time, but opening several at once adds enquiries and repayments you must still afford in January. Use one card, keep the balance low and pay in full when you can.**

## How store cards affect your record

A store card is a credit agreement. Each application adds an enquiry, and each card reports your payments every month. Paid on time, a store card helps build your record. Missed or maxed out, it does the opposite.

## Buy now pay later

Buy now pay later splits a purchase into a few instalments. Some providers check your credit and report to bureaus, others do not. Read the terms: a missed instalment can mean fees, and if the provider reports it, it can show on your record.

## Festive season rules of thumb

1. **One new account at most.** Several applications in December add enquiries that stay for up to a year.
2. **Budget for January.** School fees, back-to-school costs and the long wait to January payday all hit at once.
3. **Keep balances low.** Aim to stay under about a third of each limit.
4. **Pay more than the minimum.** Store card interest adds up quickly.
5. **Do not ignore a missed payment.** Call the store before it becomes three missed months, which is when you can be listed.

## Already in trouble?

If you are already behind on accounts, start with your free credit report. See [how to get it](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa). Then follow [the 90-day plan](https://clearmy.name/blog/improve-credit-score-90-days). If repayments are more than you can manage, talk to us before you stop paying anything.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is it good to have a store card for my credit score?

One store card paid on time can help, especially if you have little credit history. Several at once usually hurts.

### Does buy now pay later show on my credit report?

It depends on the provider. Some report to the bureaus and some do not. Check the terms before you use it.

### Will closing a store card improve my score?

Not usually. Paying it off and keeping it open with a zero balance often helps more.

Blog Post Title: Debt Collector Calling About an Old Debt? Check If It Has Prescribed
Meta description: A debt collector calling about an old account? In South Africa, most unsecured debts prescribe after 3 years. How to check, what not to say, and why paying R50 can restart the clock.
Meta Image Alt text: Person checking an old debt letter
Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**In South Africa, most ordinary unsecured debts prescribe after 3 years if you have not paid anything, have not acknowledged the debt in writing, and no summons was served on you. A prescribed debt may not be collected or listed on your credit report. Before you pay anything on an old debt, check the dates.**

## What "prescribed" means

Under the Prescription Act, most debts such as store cards, personal loans and cellphone accounts fall away after 3 years if the creditor has not acted. The National Credit Act also says a creditor may not sell or try to collect a debt that has prescribed, and prescribed debts may not be listed on your credit record.

## What stops or restarts the clock

- A payment towards the debt, even a small one
- Acknowledging the debt in writing, for example signing an acknowledgement of debt
- A summons being served on you

This is why some collectors ask for "just R50 to show goodwill". Get the facts before you pay or sign anything.

## How to check

1. Ask the collector, in writing, for the date of your last payment and the account history.
2. Check your credit report for the account and its dates. See [how to get it for free](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa).
3. Check whether a judgment was ever granted. A judgment debt has a much longer prescription period.

Our guides to [prescribed accounts](https://clearmy.name/prescribed-accounts) and [prescribed debt and credit records](https://clearmy.name/prescribed-debt-and-credit-records) include a message template you can send.

## If it has prescribed

- Tell the collector in writing that the debt has prescribed and that they must stop collecting.
- Dispute any listing of the debt on your credit report.
- If collection continues, you can complain to the National Credit Regulator or the National Financial Ombud Scheme.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long before a debt prescribes in South Africa?

Most ordinary debts prescribe after 3 years. Judgment debts and some others have longer periods.

### Can a prescribed debt stay on my credit report?

No. A debt that has prescribed may not be listed. Dispute it if it is showing.

### Does a phone call acknowledging the debt restart prescription?

Prescription is interrupted by a written acknowledgement, a payment or a summons. Avoid paying or signing anything until you have checked the dates.

Author: Clear My Name team
Blog Post Content:
**Start the year by getting your free credit reports, disputing anything wrong, bringing every account up to date and setting a simple plan to pay on time and keep balances low. Most people see a real difference within 3 to 6 months.**

## Your 10-step checklist

1. **Get your free reports** from all four bureaus. [Here is how.](https://clearmy.name/blog/check-credit-report-free-south-africa)
2. **Check your personal details** for addresses or employers you do not recognise.
3. **Dispute anything wrong**, including accounts that are not yours and paid accounts showing a balance.
4. **Check the dates** of every negative item against [the legal periods](https://clearmy.name/blog/how-long-negative-information-stays-credit-report).
5. **Check old debts** for prescription before paying a collector. [Here is why.](https://clearmy.name/blog/old-debt-collector-prescribed-debt)
6. **Bring every active account up to date** and set debit orders for at least the minimum.
7. **Pay down card balances** to under about a third of each limit.
8. **Pause new applications** for at least three months.
9. **Build if you are starting out.** [One small account, paid on time.](https://clearmy.name/blog/build-credit-record-no-credit-history)
10. **Check again in 3 months** to make sure disputes were fixed and payments are showing.

## Planning a big application in 2027?

If you want vehicle finance or a home loan this year, start now. Lenders want 6 to 12 months of clean payments and an affordable repayment.
